title: Palette of navigation primitives and journey maps
content:
Purpose:
This note pulls together a discrete set of navigation primitives (patterns we can mix-and-match) and a compact set of user journey maps to drive the console IA rewrite. Intended to be actionable for a lightweight prototype we can user-test next quarter.

Principles (short):
- Minimize cognitive leaps: surface the task, not the feature.
- Collapse complexity with progressive disclosure (micro-contexts).
- Routes should be composable and bookmarkable (URL contract).
- Make the default path good for new users; let power users opt-in to denser surfaces.

Navigation primitives (palette):
1) Edge rail (compact): primary verbs + global context. Small footprint, persistent. Use for quick route switching (Projects, Models, Jobs, Billing).
2) Column-stack (task-driven): when a workflow spans multiple vertical surfaces (select -> configure -> run), present as stacked columns with explicit step anchors.
3) Surface cards (workbench): density-first surface for lists and quick actions; supports inline expansion for previews and KV cache stats.
4) Flyout routing (task-scoped): transient context panel anchored to list rows/modal triggers; not a full route but has its own breadcrumb shard.
5) Deep-link tabs: sub-route tabs that represent stateful filters or modes (Logs | Metrics | Traces) and map 1:1 to URL fragments.
6) Floating quick-open: command-palette style for power navigation (command + k).

Routing contracts / URL shape guidance:
- Root paths should be resource-centric: /projects/:projectId/models/:modelId/...
- Use query params for ephemeral filters: ?q=bert&status=running
- Tabs -> /path/to/resource?mode=metrics (explicit) or /path/to/resource/metrics (preferable for back/forward semantics) — propose /resource/:id/mode to support deep sharing.
- Flyouts: /resource/:id?panel=preview -> but prefer /resource/:id/preview to keep history tidy.

Page hierarchy recommendations:
- Level 1: Workspace (Projects) - global affordances (billing, org settings).
- Level 2: Resource collection (Models, Endpoints, Runs) - filtered, sortable lists.
- Level 3: Resource detail - primary entity view with nav to related slices (metrics, logs, versions).
- Level 4: Task surface (create/edit/preview) - modal or column-stack depending on complexity.

Journey maps (3 canonical users):
A) New Developer - goal: get a simple text-generation demo running in 15 minutes. Key needs: clear entrypoint, minimal choices, ephemeral defaults. Recommended path: Projects -> Create demo project (guided) -> Hosted API quickstart -> CLI token modal -> Example app.
B) Platform Engineer - goal: pin a model version and configure rollout policy. Needs: predictable routes, compare views, rollouts page. Recommended primitives: column-stack for compare; deep-link tabs for rollout history; edge rail for global route switching.
C) SRE / Troubleshooter - goal: find why tail latency spiked. Needs: dense drilldowns, metrics-first landing, logs inlined. Recommended primitives: surface cards + flyout routing for traces, deep-link tabs for logs/metrics/traces.

Transition & migration strategy:
- Phase 0 (experiment): build prototype for two flows (New Developer, Platform Engineer) using a hybrid edge-rail + column-stack layout. Run moderated usability tests (N=6 each).
- Phase 1 (opt-in): behind feature flag, enable new rail for 10% of orgs; collect route telemetry and task completion metrics.
- Phase 2 (migrate): provide an automated mapping for legacy routes -> new routes; keep legacy alias redirects for 6 months.

Accessibility and performance constraints:
- Ensure keyboard focus order follows column-stack to preserve sequential mental model.
- Limit animation durations and prefer transform-based transitions to avoid jank on lower-end devices.
- Landmark roles for rail and main content; aria-expanded for flyouts.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Tabs-as-path vs tabs-as-query: prefer path for shareability, but search & link tooling depends on query. Need infra input. (Action: eng to confirm routing layer capabilities; see jira PROD-1284).
- Flyouts in history: should opening a flyout create a history entry? Pros: back navigation; Cons: history spam. Lean: create history entry for heavy actions (edit, promote) but not for preview.
- How dense should default rail be? compact icons-only vs labeled. Lean: icons+condensed labels on first load; collapse to icons for power users.

Prototype plan & next steps:
- Kickoff wireframe sprint (2 designers, 1 PM, 1 eng prototype) - 2 weeks. Deliverables: Figma prototype, clickthrough user test script, route contract doc.
- Usability tests: recruit 12 participants across three personas; run moderated sessions and record success metrics.
- Follow-up grooming: convert successful primitives into tickets, prioritize by impact and engineering cost.

Appendix: quick heuristics for picking primitives:
- Single-turn tasks -> flyout or quick modal.
- Multi-step config -> column-stack.
- High-frequency route switching -> edge rail.
- Data-dense troubleshooting -> surface cards + deep-link tabs.

Notes to self:
- Sync with SRE on metrics-per-route instrumentation (Evan).
- Confirm multi-org routing edgecases with backend (Diego).
- Add a small glossary of route terms before prototype handoff.

---
This is intentionally condensed; we should expand the route contract section into a spec once the prototype tests validate assumptions.
